title: Release publish is gated on a manual npm-publish environment approval; v1.34.0 was tagged but never published
observation: Observed 2026-09-14. release.yml's publish job runs in the GitHub environment `npm-publish`, which requires a reviewer approval. The v1.34.0 tag push (12:56) produced a run whose validate and platform jobs passed, then sat in `waiting` for two hours; npm `latest` stayed at 1.33.0 while README, site and CHANGELOG announced 1.34.0. The v1.35.0 run hit the same gate. Resolution: the stale 1.34.0 deployment was rejected (publishing it after 1.35.0 would have moved `latest` backwards; 1.35.0 contains every 1.34.0 change), the 1.35.0 deployment was approved with David's explicit instruction, publish completed, npm latest = 1.35.0 with SLSA v1 provenance. The release runbook (rb_cut_release_01) does not mention this approval step, so an unattended or agent-driven release stalls silently after the tag push. Follow-ups: add the approval step (and `gh api -X POST .../actions/runs/<id>/pending_deployments -F environment_ids[]=18609597918 -f state=approved`) to the runbook; consider a release-gate check that fails loudly when a version tag exists whose npm publish has not happened within N minutes; note in CHANGELOG that 1.34.0 was superseded before publication (PR #234).
